name: Maximum-Generated Closure for Monotone Path Fibers
statement: Let two maximum-generated classes on disjoint private blocks share the path $00,10,11$. If each triple of private fibers is nested in either path orientation, their coordinate fiber product over the path is maximum-generated. The orientations may agree or be opposite, and consecutive fibers may coincide.
proof: For opposite orientations, cumulative-path certificates turn the visible nested fibers into marked sections of actual opposite consecutive maximum triples, to which the triple-parent construction applies. For equal orientations, first use one-coordinate product closure over one path coordinate and then projection--reduction gluing to install the remaining lowest fiber. Equal visible fibers do not affect the consecutive ranks of the ambient certificates.
comments: General path gluing remains open because the two cumulative certificates need not be simultaneous.
